questions.question: A developer needs to set up an SSL security certificate for a client’s eCommerce website in order to use the HTTPS protocol. Which of the following AWS services can be used to deploy the required SSL server certificates? (Choose TWO)

explanation.summary: Amazon Route 53 can be used to route HTTPS traffic to resources that use SSL/TLS certificates, making it part of deploying secure web applications.
keyPoints: Route 53 is a highly available and scalable DNS service
It supports routing traffic to HTTPS-enabled endpoints
Works with SSL/TLS certificates attached to AWS resources
Integrates with services like CloudFront and ALB
Used to configure DNS records for secure websites
examples: Routing HTTPS traffic to an Application Load Balancer that uses an ACM certificate
Pointing a domain name to a CloudFront distribution secured with SSL
Managing DNS for an eCommerce website using HTTPS
explanation.additionalInfo: Route 53 itself does not generate SSL certificates, but it plays a critical role in deploying SSL-enabled websites by routing users to AWS resources that use SSL certificates. In exam scenarios, Route 53 is often paired with ACM because ACM provisions the certificate while Route 53 helps validate domains and route secure traffic. This combination is commonly tested in foundational AWS exams.

explanation.summary: AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) is the primary AWS service used to provision, manage, and deploy SSL/TLS certificates.
keyPoints: Integrates with ELB, CloudFront, and API Gateway
examples: Provisioning an SSL certificate for an ALB
Using ACM with CloudFront for HTTPS
Automatically renewing certificates for an eCommerce site
explanation.additionalInfo: ACM is the correct and most direct service for deploying SSL server certificates in AWS. It removes the operational burden of certificate creation, renewal, and rotation. For exam questions, ACM is almost always the correct choice when SSL/TLS certificates are mentioned, especially for HTTPS websites.

explanation.summary: AWS Directory Service is used for managing Microsoft Active Directory and does not manage SSL certificates.
explanation.why: Directory Service focuses on identity management and authentication, not web encryption or HTTPS certificates.

explanation.summary: IAM manages users, roles, and permissions, not SSL server certificates.
explanation.why: IAM controls access to AWS resources but does not handle HTTPS encryption or certificate deployment.

explanation.summary: AWS Data Pipeline is used for data movement and processing workflows, not security certificates.
explanation.why: It is unrelated to HTTPS, SSL, or web security use cases.

questions.question: Which of the following AWS services scale automatically without your intervention? (Choose TWO)

explanation.summary: Amazon EC2 does not scale automatically by default.
explanation.why: EC2 requires Auto Scaling groups or manual intervention to scale compute capacity.

explanation.summary: Amazon S3 automatically scales storage capacity as data is added or removed.
examples: Handling traffic spikes for static websites
Growing log storage without manual scaling
explanation.additionalInfo: S3 is a core example of an AWS service that scales transparently. Users never provision storage size. This concept is frequently tested to distinguish managed services from infrastructure services.

explanation.summary: AWS Lambda automatically scales compute execution in response to events.
explanation.additionalInfo: Lambda is a core serverless service. AWS handles all scaling, concurrency, and infrastructure concerns. In exams, Lambda is always associated with automatic scaling.

explanation.summary: Amazon EMR clusters do not automatically scale unless configured.
explanation.why: Scaling requires auto-scaling policies or manual configuration.

explanation.summary: Amazon EBS volumes do not scale automatically.
explanation.why: Storage size and performance must be manually adjusted.

questions.question: A company is planning to migrate an application from Amazon EC2 to AWS Lambda to use a serverless architecture. Which of the following will be the responsibility of AWS after migration? (Choose TWO)

explanation.summary: Application logic remains the customer’s responsibility.
explanation.why: AWS manages infrastructure, not application code or business logic.

explanation.summary: AWS manages capacity automatically in Lambda.
examples: Scaling from one to thousands of requests
explanation.additionalInfo: In Lambda, capacity management is fully abstracted. This is a defining characteristic of serverless computing and a frequent exam topic.

explanation.summary: Access control remains the customer’s responsibility.
explanation.why: IAM roles and permissions must be defined by the customer.

explanation.summary: AWS manages the operating system in Lambda.
explanation.additionalInfo: In serverless services, the OS layer is fully managed by AWS. This is a clear distinction from EC2 and commonly tested in certification exams.

explanation.summary: Customers remain responsible for data management.
explanation.why: AWS manages infrastructure, not application data lifecycle or integrity.

questions.question: How do ELBs improve the reliability of your application?

options.text: By distributing traffic across multiple S3 buckets.

explanation.summary: Elastic Load Balancers do not distribute traffic to Amazon S3 buckets.
explanation.why: ELBs route traffic to compute targets such as EC2 instances, containers, or Lambda functions. S3 is an object storage service and does not receive traffic through ELBs.

options.text: By replicating data to multiple availability zones.

explanation.summary: Data replication across Availability Zones is not performed by ELBs.
explanation.why: ELBs distribute network traffic but do not replicate application data. Data replication is handled by services such as Amazon RDS, DynamoDB, or S3.

explanation.summary: Database Read Replicas are created by database services, not ELBs.
explanation.why: Read Replicas are a feature of services like Amazon RDS and Amazon Aurora. ELBs do not manage databases or replication.

options.text: By ensuring that only healthy targets receive traffic.

explanation.summary: ELBs improve application reliability by routing traffic only to healthy targets.
keyPoints: Automatically stop routing traffic to unhealthy targets
Distribute traffic across multiple Availability Zones
Managed and highly available by default
examples: Stopping traffic to failed EC2 instances
Maintaining service availability during instance crashes
explanation.additionalInfo: Elastic Load Balancing is a core reliability service in AWS architectures. By performing regular health checks and dynamically adjusting traffic distribution, ELBs prevent failed instances from impacting end users. This behavior is central to AWS high-availability designs and is frequently tested in certification exams.

questions.question: A company needs to migrate their website from on-premises to AWS. Security is a major concern for them, so they need to host their website on hardware that is NOT shared with other AWS customers. Which of the following EC2 instance options meets this requirement?

explanation.summary: On-demand instances run on shared hardware by default.
explanation.why: On-demand pricing affects billing flexibility, not hardware isolation. Instances may still share underlying physical hosts with other customers.

explanation.summary: Spot instances do not provide dedicated hardware.
explanation.why: Spot instances use spare EC2 capacity and still run on shared infrastructure. They also come with interruption risk.

explanation.summary: Dedicated instances run on hardware that is dedicated to a single customer.
keyPoints: Physical server is not shared with other customers
Meets strict compliance and security requirements
Instances may still share hardware within the same account
Higher cost compared to shared tenancy
examples: Running workloads with strict compliance needs
explanation.additionalInfo: Dedicated Instances provide hardware isolation at the host level. While they are more expensive than shared tenancy, they are commonly chosen when compliance or security policies prohibit multi-tenant infrastructure. Exams often test the distinction between Dedicated Instances and Dedicated Hosts.

explanation.summary: Reserved Instances provide billing discounts, not hardware isolation.
explanation.why: Reservation affects pricing commitment only. Hardware may still be shared unless dedicated tenancy is explicitly selected.

questions.question: A customer is planning to move billions of images and videos to be stored on Amazon S3. The customer has approximately 60 Petabytes of data to move. Which of the following AWS Services is the best choice to transfer the data to AWS?

explanation.summary: Snowball is not ideal for extremely large-scale data transfers like tens of petabytes.
explanation.why: Snowball devices are suitable for terabyte to low-petabyte transfers, but not for massive multi-petabyte migrations.

explanation.summary: S3 Transfer Acceleration is designed for internet-based transfers, not massive offline migrations.
explanation.why: Moving 60 PB over the internet would take too long and be impractical, even with acceleration.

explanation.summary: AWS Snowmobile is designed to transfer extremely large amounts of data, up to exabytes.
keyPoints: Supports transfers of up to 100 PB per Snowmobile
explanation.additionalInfo: Snowmobile is the correct choice for very large data transfers measured in tens of petabytes or more. Exams commonly distinguish Snowball (TBs to small PBs) from Snowmobile (10s of PBs to exabytes).

explanation.summary: Amazon VPC is a networking service and does not transfer data.
explanation.why: VPC provides network isolation but does not move large datasets into AWS.

questions.question: A company plans to migrate a large amount of archived data to AWS. The archived data must be maintained for a period of 5 years and must be retrievable within 5 hours of a request. What is the most cost-effective AWS storage service to use?

explanation.summary: Amazon S3 Glacier is designed for low-cost archival storage with retrieval times that meet the stated requirement.
keyPoints: Lowest-cost storage option for long-term archives
Supports retrieval within minutes to hours
Ideal for compliance and long-term retention
explanation.additionalInfo: Amazon S3 Glacier is commonly tested in exam scenarios involving long-term data retention with relaxed access time requirements. Retrieval options include expedited, standard, and bulk, allowing organizations to balance cost and access speed. For a 5-hour retrieval requirement, Glacier is a cost-optimal choice compared to S3 Standard or EBS.

explanation.summary: Amazon EFS is a high-performance file system and not suitable for low-cost archival storage.
explanation.why: EFS is designed for shared file access with frequent reads and writes and is significantly more expensive than archival storage classes.

explanation.summary: Amazon S3 Standard is not the most cost-effective option for archived data.
explanation.why: S3 Standard is optimized for frequent access and has higher storage costs than archival tiers like Glacier.

explanation.summary: Amazon EBS is block storage intended for active workloads, not archives.
explanation.why: EBS volumes are costly and require attached EC2 instances, making them unsuitable for long-term archived data.

questions.question: Which AWS Service is used to manage user permissions?

explanation.summary: Security Groups control network traffic, not user permissions.
explanation.why: They act as virtual firewalls for resources and do not manage identities or access rights.

explanation.summary: Amazon ECS is a container orchestration service, not an identity management service.
explanation.why: ECS manages containers and tasks, while user permissions are handled by IAM.

explanation.summary: AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) is used to manage user permissions in AWS.
explanation.additionalInfo: IAM is a foundational AWS service and is heavily tested in certification exams. It enables centralized access control and is core to AWS security best practices. Questions involving permissions, authentication, or authorization almost always point to IAM.

explanation.summary: AWS Support provides technical assistance, not permission management.
explanation.why: Support plans do not control or manage access to AWS resources.

questions.question: Which support plan includes AWS Support Concierge Service?

explanation.summary: Premium Support is not an official AWS support plan name.
explanation.why: AWS support plans are Basic, Developer, Business, and Enterprise.

explanation.summary: Business Support does not include Concierge Service.
explanation.why: Concierge support is exclusive to the Enterprise Support plan.

explanation.summary: Enterprise Support includes AWS Support Concierge Service.
keyPoints: 24x7 access to senior cloud support engineers
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS Support Concierge Service is specifically associated with the Enterprise Support plan. This is a common exam question that tests knowledge of AWS support tiers and their benefits.

explanation.summary: Standard Support is not an AWS support plan tier.
explanation.why: AWS does not offer a plan named Standard Support.

questions.question: A company needs to track resource changes using the API call history. Which AWS service can help the company achieve this goal?

explanation.summary: AWS Config tracks configuration changes, not API call history.
explanation.why: Config records the state and compliance of resources over time, but it does not log who made API calls or when.

explanation.summary: Amazon CloudWatch focuses on metrics, logs, and alarms, not API auditing.
explanation.why: While CloudWatch can store logs and metrics, it does not natively record AWS API call history.

explanation.summary: AWS CloudTrail records API calls made in an AWS account.
keyPoints: Records who made the call and when
explanation.additionalInfo: CloudTrail is the primary service for tracking API activity in AWS. It provides a detailed event history that includes the identity of the caller, the time of the request, and the affected resources. In certification exams, any question involving API call history, auditing, or tracking user actions points directly to CloudTrail.

explanation.summary: AWS CloudFormation is an infrastructure provisioning service.
explanation.why: It deploys and manages resources as code but does not track API call history or user actions.

questions.question: What are the benefits of using an AWS-managed service? (Choose TWO)

options.text: Provides complete control over the virtual infrastructure.

explanation.summary: AWS-managed services reduce control in exchange for simplicity.
explanation.why: Managed services abstract infrastructure management, limiting low-level control over servers and operating systems.

options.text: Allows customers to deliver new solutions faster.

explanation.summary: AWS-managed services accelerate development by removing infrastructure management.
explanation.additionalInfo: Managed services shift operational responsibilities to AWS, allowing teams to focus on building features instead of managing infrastructure. This benefit is frequently highlighted in exam questions about agility and time-to-market.

explanation.summary: AWS-managed services reduce operational burden.
examples: Using Amazon RDS instead of self-managed databases
explanation.additionalInfo: Lower operational complexity is one of the strongest arguments for managed services. Exams often contrast this benefit against self-managed solutions on EC2.

options.text: Eliminates the need to encrypt data.

explanation.summary: Encryption is still required when using managed services.
explanation.why: Security responsibilities are shared, and customers must ensure data protection.

options.text: Allows developers to control all patching related activities.

explanation.summary: Patching is typically handled by AWS in managed services.
explanation.why: Managed services remove the need for customers to manage OS or service-level patching.

questions.question: Which of the following are use cases for Amazon S3? (Choose TWO)

explanation.summary: Amazon S3 can host static websites directly.
examples: Hosting HTML, CSS, and JavaScript sites
explanation.additionalInfo: S3 static website hosting is a common exam topic and highlights S3’s role beyond simple storage.

learnMore.title: Hosting a Static Website on Amazon S3

options.text: Hosting websites that require sustained high CPU utilization.

explanation.summary: Amazon S3 does not provide compute resources.
explanation.why: High CPU workloads require services like EC2 or containers, not object storage.

explanation.summary: S3 is not a database service.
explanation.why: While logs can be stored in S3, it is not used as a database replacement in exam contexts.

options.text: A media store for the CloudFront service.

explanation.summary: Amazon S3 is commonly used as an origin for Amazon CloudFront.
explanation.additionalInfo: Using S3 with CloudFront is a standard AWS architecture pattern and frequently appears in exam questions.

options.text: Processing data streams at any scale.

explanation.summary: Data stream processing is handled by services like Kinesis.
explanation.why: S3 stores objects and does not process streaming data in real time.

questions.question: What is the AWS’ recommendation regarding access keys?

options.text: Delete all access keys and use passwords instead.

explanation.summary: AWS does not recommend replacing access keys with passwords.
explanation.why: Passwords are used for console access, while access keys are required for programmatic access.

options.text: Only share them with trusted people.

explanation.summary: AWS does not recommend sharing access keys at all.
explanation.why: Access keys are sensitive credentials and must never be shared, even with trusted individuals.

explanation.summary: AWS recommends rotating access keys regularly to reduce security risk.
keyPoints: Limits exposure if keys are compromised
examples: Rotating IAM user access keys every 90 days
Replacing long-term keys with IAM roles
Auditing unused keys and disabling them
explanation.additionalInfo: Regular key rotation is a core IAM best practice and is frequently tested in AWS exams. AWS also strongly recommends using IAM roles and temporary credentials instead of long-term access keys whenever possible.

learnMore.title: Best Practices for Managing AWS Access Keys

options.text: Save them within your application code.

explanation.summary: Storing access keys in application code is insecure.
explanation.why: Hard-coded credentials increase the risk of accidental exposure and compromise.

questions.question: What is the AWS IAM feature that provides an additional layer of security on top of user-name and password authentication?

explanation.summary: Key pairs are used for EC2 instance access, not IAM authentication.
explanation.why: They provide SSH access to instances but do not add a second authentication factor to IAM users.

explanation.summary: Access keys enable programmatic access, not multi-factor authentication.
explanation.why: They are credentials themselves and do not provide an additional authentication layer.

explanation.summary: SDKs are development tools, not security features.
explanation.why: They help interact with AWS services programmatically but do not provide authentication layers.

explanation.summary: Multi-Factor Authentication adds an extra security layer beyond username and password.
keyPoints: Strongly recommended for root and IAM users
examples: Hardware MFA devices for root users
Enforcing MFA for privileged IAM users
explanation.additionalInfo: MFA is one of the most emphasized security best practices in AWS exams. Any question asking for an additional layer of authentication almost always points to MFA.

questions.question: What is the benefit of using an API to access AWS Services?

options.text: It improves the performance of AWS resources.

explanation.summary: APIs do not directly improve resource performance.
explanation.why: Performance depends on service configuration and architecture, not access method.

options.text: It reduces the time needed to provision AWS resources.

explanation.summary: APIs enable automation but do not inherently reduce provisioning time.
explanation.why: Provisioning speed is determined by the service, not whether APIs or console are used.

options.text: It reduces the number of developers necessary.

explanation.summary: APIs do not affect team size.
explanation.why: They provide access methods but do not replace development or operational roles.

options.text: It allows for programmatic management of AWS resources.

explanation.summary: APIs enable programmatic control and automation of AWS resources.
explanation.additionalInfo: APIs are fundamental to AWS automation. Services like CloudFormation, SDKs, and CLI all rely on AWS APIs. Exams often frame APIs as the enabler for automation and infrastructure as code.

questions.question: A company is planning to migrate a database with high read/write activity to AWS. What is the best storage option to use?

explanation.summary: AWS Storage Gateway is designed for hybrid storage, not high-performance database workloads.
explanation.why: Storage Gateway connects on-premises environments to AWS storage services and does not provide low-latency block storage required for databases.

explanation.summary: Amazon S3 is object storage and not suitable for database workloads.
explanation.why: Databases require low-latency block storage with frequent read/write operations, which S3 does not provide.

explanation.summary: Amazon EBS provides high-performance block storage suitable for databases with high read/write activity.
examples: Running MySQL or PostgreSQL on EC2
explanation.additionalInfo: Amazon EBS is the standard storage choice for databases running on EC2. Provisioned IOPS volumes are specifically designed for I/O-intensive workloads. In exams, high read/write database scenarios almost always map to EBS.

explanation.summary: Amazon Glacier is designed for archival storage, not active databases.
explanation.why: Glacier has long retrieval times and is unsuitable for frequent read/write access.

questions.question: How can AWS customers track and avoid over-spending on underutilized reserved instances?

options.text: Customers can add all AWS accounts to an AWS Organization, enable Consolidated Billing, and turn off Reserved Instance sharing.

explanation.summary: This approach does not directly track or alert on underutilized Reserved Instances.
explanation.why: Consolidated billing and RI sharing settings do not provide utilization monitoring or cost alerts.

options.text: Customers can use Amazon Neptune to track and analyze their usage patterns, detect underutilized reserved instances, and then sell them on the Amazon EC2 Reserved Instance Marketplace.

explanation.summary: Amazon Neptune is a graph database and unrelated to cost tracking.
explanation.why: Neptune does not provide billing analysis or Reserved Instance utilization insights.

options.text: Customers can use the AWS Budgets service to track the reserved instances usage and set up alert notifications when their utilization drops below the threshold that they define.

explanation.summary: AWS Budgets allows tracking Reserved Instance utilization and alerts on underuse.
keyPoints: Sends alerts via email or SNS
examples: Alert when RI utilization drops below 80%
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS Budgets is the correct service for proactive cost control. Exam questions involving alerts, thresholds, and cost tracking almost always point to AWS Budgets.

options.text: Customers can use Amazon CloudTrail to automatically check for unused reservations and get recommendations to reduce their bill.

explanation.summary: CloudTrail tracks API activity, not cost optimization.
explanation.why: It does not analyze Reserved Instance utilization or provide billing recommendations.

questions.question: What is the AWS service that provides five times the performance of a standard MySQL database?

explanation.summary: Amazon Aurora delivers up to five times the performance of standard MySQL databases.
explanation.additionalInfo: Aurora is frequently tested in exams for its performance claims. AWS explicitly states that Aurora provides up to five times the throughput of standard MySQL on the same hardware.

explanation.summary: Amazon Redshift is a data warehouse, not a MySQL-compatible OLTP database.
explanation.why: Redshift is optimized for analytics workloads, not transactional databases.

explanation.summary: DynamoDB is a NoSQL database and not MySQL-compatible.
explanation.why: It does not use SQL or relational schemas and is not compared directly to MySQL performance.

explanation.summary: Amazon Neptune is a graph database.
explanation.why: It is designed for graph workloads, not relational MySQL performance comparisons.

questions.question: What does AWS Service Catalog provide?

options.text: It enables customers to quickly find descriptions and use cases for AWS services.

explanation.summary: AWS Service Catalog is not a general service discovery tool.
explanation.why: Service descriptions and use cases are provided through AWS documentation and the AWS website, not Service Catalog.

options.text: It enables customers to explore the different catalogs of AWS services.

explanation.summary: Service Catalog does not list all AWS services.
explanation.why: It is used to manage approved IT services, not to browse the entire AWS service portfolio.

options.text: It simplifies organizing and governing commonly deployed IT services.

explanation.summary: AWS Service Catalog allows organizations to centrally manage and govern approved IT services.
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS Service Catalog is commonly tested as a governance tool. It enables organizations to balance self-service access with centralized control, which is critical in large enterprises.

options.text: It allows developers to deploy infrastructure on AWS using familiar programming languages.

explanation.summary: This description aligns more closely with AWS CDK.
explanation.why: Service Catalog uses predefined templates rather than developer-written infrastructure code.

questions.question: For managed services like Amazon DynamoDB, which of the below is AWS responsible for? (Choose TWO)

explanation.summary: Credential protection is the customer’s responsibility.
explanation.why: Customers must secure IAM users, roles, and access keys under the shared responsibility model.

explanation.summary: Access logging configuration is typically a customer responsibility.
explanation.why: Customers must enable and configure logging services such as CloudTrail and CloudWatch.

explanation.summary: AWS manages database software patching for DynamoDB.
explanation.additionalInfo: For fully managed services like DynamoDB, AWS is responsible for maintaining and patching the underlying service software. This is a core exam concept tied to the shared responsibility model.

explanation.summary: AWS manages the operating system for managed services.
explanation.additionalInfo: Managed services abstract the operating system entirely. This is a frequent exam distinction between EC2-based workloads and managed services.

explanation.summary: Access policies are defined by the customer.
explanation.why: IAM policies and permissions must be created and managed by the customer.

questions.question: Which of the following AWS Services helps with planning application migration to the AWS Cloud?

explanation.summary: Snowball is used for data transfer, not migration planning.
explanation.why: It moves data but does not analyze applications or environments.

explanation.summary: AWS Application Discovery Service helps plan migrations by collecting on-premises data.
explanation.additionalInfo: Application Discovery Service is specifically designed for the assessment and planning phase of migrations. Exams often test it alongside Migration Hub and DMS.

explanation.summary: AWS DMS is used to migrate databases, not plan migrations.
explanation.why: It executes migrations rather than discovering or assessing workloads.

explanation.summary: Migration Hub tracks migration progress rather than performing discovery.
explanation.why: It provides visibility but relies on discovery tools for planning data.

questions.question: A company is trying to analyze the costs applied to their AWS account recently. Which of the following provides them the most granular data about their AWS costs and usage?

explanation.summary: An Amazon Machine Image does not provide cost or usage data.
explanation.why: AMIs are templates for launching EC2 instances and have no billing or usage analytics capabilities.

explanation.summary: AWS Cost Explorer provides summarized and visualized cost data, not the most granular level.
explanation.why: While useful for trends and analysis, it does not expose the full line-item detail available in cost reports.

explanation.summary: The AWS Cost & Usage Report provides the most detailed cost and usage data available.
keyPoints: Integrates with Amazon Athena and S3
examples: Breaking down costs by service and usage type
explanation.additionalInfo: The Cost & Usage Report is the authoritative source for AWS billing data. It is commonly tested as the most granular and comprehensive billing tool, especially when compared to Cost Explorer or Budgets.

explanation.summary: Amazon CloudWatch monitors metrics and logs, not billing data.
explanation.why: It tracks performance and operational metrics rather than cost and usage details.

questions.question: Which statement best describes the concept of an AWS region?

options.text: An AWS Region is a geographical location with a collection of Edge locations.

explanation.summary: Edge locations are part of CloudFront, not the definition of a Region.
explanation.why: Regions consist of Availability Zones, while edge locations are separate global endpoints.

options.text: An AWS Region is a virtual network dedicated only to a single AWS customer.

explanation.summary: This description applies to Amazon VPC, not Regions.
explanation.why: A VPC is a logically isolated network, while a Region is a physical geographic area.

options.text: An AWS Region is a geographical location with a collection of Availability Zones.

explanation.summary: An AWS Region consists of multiple, isolated Availability Zones within a geographic area.
explanation.additionalInfo: Understanding the distinction between Regions and Availability Zones is fundamental for AWS exams. Regions provide geographic isolation, while AZs enable high availability within a Region.

options.text: An AWS Region represents the country where the AWS infrastructure exist.

explanation.summary: AWS Regions are not defined by country boundaries.
explanation.why: A single country can contain multiple Regions, and Regions can span broader geographic areas.

questions.question: A company has discovered that multiple S3 buckets were deleted, but it is unclear who deleted the buckets. Which of the following can the company use to determine the identity that deleted the buckets?

explanation.summary: SNS does not log API activity or user actions.
explanation.why: SNS is a messaging service and does not provide audit logs for resource deletions.

explanation.summary: SQS does not track resource deletion actions.
explanation.why: It manages message queues and does not audit API calls.

explanation.summary: CloudWatch Logs store logs sent by services or applications, not API call history by default.
explanation.why: Without CloudTrail integration, CloudWatch Logs cannot identify who deleted AWS resources.

explanation.summary: AWS CloudTrail logs record who performed API actions such as deleting S3 buckets.
examples: Identifying who deleted an S3 bucket
explanation.additionalInfo: Any exam question asking who performed an action in AWS points directly to CloudTrail. It is the definitive audit trail service for AWS accounts.

questions.question: Which of the following are factors in determining the appropriate database technology to use for a specific workload? (Choose TWO)

explanation.summary: Availability Zones relate to deployment architecture, not database selection criteria.
explanation.why: AZs affect availability and fault tolerance, but they do not determine whether a relational, NoSQL, or other database technology is appropriate.

explanation.summary: Data sovereignty affects region selection, not database technology choice.
explanation.why: It determines where data must reside geographically, but not the type of database engine required.

options.text: The number of reads and writes per second.

explanation.summary: Read and write throughput requirements are a key factor in database selection.
keyPoints: Helps choose between relational and NoSQL
explanation.additionalInfo: Throughput requirements strongly influence whether a workload is better suited to services like DynamoDB or traditional relational databases. This is a common exam decision-making criterion.

learnMore.title: Choosing the Right Database on AWS

explanation.summary: Query complexity and access patterns are fundamental to database technology selection.
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS exams frequently emphasize access patterns and query types as the primary drivers for choosing between database technologies.

explanation.summary: Software bugs are not a database selection factor.
explanation.why: Bugs relate to application quality, not the underlying database technology choice.

questions.question: What are the benefits of implementing a tagging strategy for AWS resources? (Choose TWO)

options.text: Quickly identify resources that belong to a specific project.

explanation.summary: Tags enable logical grouping of resources by project, environment, or owner.
explanation.additionalInfo: Tagging is a foundational governance practice in AWS. Exams often test tagging as a mechanism for organization and cost tracking.

options.text: Quickly identify software solutions on AWS.

explanation.summary: Tags are applied to resources, not software solutions.
explanation.why: Software discovery is handled through AWS Marketplace and documentation, not resource tags.

options.text: Track API calls in your AWS account.

explanation.summary: API tracking is handled by CloudTrail, not tagging.
explanation.why: Tags do not record or audit user actions.

options.text: Quickly identify deleted resources and their metadata.

explanation.summary: Tags are not preserved after resource deletion.
explanation.why: Deleted resources and their metadata must be tracked using logs and audit services.

options.text: Track AWS spending across multiple resources.

explanation.summary: Tags enable cost allocation and spending analysis.
explanation.additionalInfo: Cost allocation tags are frequently tested in exams as a key cost management feature.

questions.question: What are AWS shared controls?

options.text: Controls that are solely the responsibility of the customer based on the application they are deploying within AWS services.

explanation.summary: This describes customer-only responsibilities.
explanation.why: Shared controls involve both AWS and the customer, not just the customer.

options.text: Controls that a customer inherits from AWS.

explanation.summary: Inherited controls are provided entirely by AWS.
explanation.why: Shared controls require joint responsibility.

options.text: Controls that apply to both the infrastructure layer and customer layers.

explanation.summary: This description is incomplete and ambiguous.
explanation.why: It does not clearly express shared operational responsibility between AWS and the customer.

options.text: Controls that the customer and AWS collaborate together upon to secure the infrastructure.

explanation.summary: AWS shared controls are responsibilities jointly managed by AWS and the customer.
explanation.additionalInfo: Shared controls are a frequent exam topic and sit between AWS-only and customer-only responsibilities in the shared responsibility model.

questions.question: Which design principles relate to performance efficiency in AWS? (Choose TWO)

options.text: Build multi-region architectures to better serve global customers.

explanation.summary: Multi-region architectures improve performance by reducing latency for global users.
keyPoints: Places resources closer to end users
examples: Serving users from the nearest AWS Region
explanation.additionalInfo: The Performance Efficiency pillar emphasizes using the right resources in the right locations. Multi-region designs are often tested as a way to improve performance for global workloads.

explanation.summary: Applying security at all layers relates to the Security pillar, not performance efficiency.
explanation.why: This principle focuses on protection rather than performance optimization.

options.text: Implement strong Identity and Access controls.

explanation.summary: Strong IAM controls belong to the Security pillar.
explanation.why: Identity controls do not directly improve system performance.

explanation.summary: Serverless architectures support performance efficiency through automatic scaling.
explanation.additionalInfo: The Performance Efficiency pillar encourages using serverless and managed services to ensure resources match demand. This is a recurring exam theme.

explanation.summary: Audit logging relates to security and governance, not performance.
explanation.why: Logging improves visibility and compliance but does not enhance performance efficiency.

questions.question: Which of the below are responsibilities of the customer when using Amazon EC2? (Choose TWO)

explanation.summary: Customers are responsible for protecting their data on EC2.
explanation.additionalInfo: Under the shared responsibility model, customers are always responsible for their data. This applies regardless of the AWS service used.

explanation.summary: AWS handles patching of the underlying infrastructure.
explanation.why: Physical data centers and host infrastructure are AWS responsibilities.

options.text: Setup and operation of managed databases.

explanation.summary: Managed databases are operated by AWS.
explanation.why: Services like Amazon RDS handle database operations, patching, and backups.

explanation.summary: Hardware maintenance is handled by AWS.
explanation.why: Customers do not manage physical servers in EC2.

explanation.summary: Customers manage the software installed on EC2 instances.
keyPoints: Full control over OS and software
explanation.additionalInfo: EC2 provides infrastructure control to customers, which includes responsibility for the software layer. This is a common exam contrast with managed services.

questions.question: Why would an organization decide to use AWS over an on-premises data center? (Choose TWO)

explanation.summary: AWS does not provide free commercial software licenses by default.
explanation.why: Licensing costs depend on the software vendor and licensing model.

explanation.summary: Technical support is not free for advanced support tiers.
explanation.why: AWS charges for Developer, Business, and Enterprise support plans.

explanation.summary: AWS provides elastic resources that scale with demand.
keyPoints: Scale up or down as needed
Pay only for what is used
explanation.additionalInfo: Elasticity is a foundational cloud benefit and frequently tested in AWS certification exams.

explanation.summary: AWS does not provide on-site audits for customers.
explanation.why: Compliance documentation is provided through AWS Artifact instead.

explanation.summary: AWS reduces costs by eliminating large upfront capital expenses.
explanation.additionalInfo: Cost savings combined with elasticity is a core reason organizations migrate to AWS. This pairing is very common in exam questions.

questions.question: Which of the following AWS services can help you perform security analysis and regulatory compliance auditing? (Choose TWO)

explanation.summary: Amazon Inspector performs automated security assessments of AWS workloads.
explanation.additionalInfo: Amazon Inspector is frequently tested as a security analysis service. It focuses on vulnerability assessment rather than logging or monitoring.

explanation.summary: A Virtual Private Gateway enables VPN connectivity.
explanation.why: It provides network connectivity but does not perform security analysis or compliance auditing.

explanation.summary: AWS Batch is used for running batch computing jobs.
explanation.why: It does not provide security or compliance analysis features.

explanation.summary: Amazon ECS is a container orchestration service.
explanation.why: It manages containers but does not analyze security posture or compliance.

explanation.summary: AWS Config enables compliance auditing and configuration tracking.
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS Config is a core compliance service. Exam questions involving regulatory auditing, configuration history, or compliance checks often point to AWS Config.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2)?

options.text: Amazon EC2 is considered a Serverless Web Service.

explanation.summary: Amazon EC2 is not a serverless service.
explanation.additionalInfo: EC2 is an Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) offering. Exams frequently test this distinction by contrasting EC2 with serverless services like AWS Lambda.

options.text: Amazon EC2 eliminates the need to invest in hardware upfront.

explanation.summary: This is a valid characteristic of EC2.
explanation.why: EC2 removes the need for upfront hardware investment by using on-demand cloud infrastructure.

options.text: Amazon EC2 can launch as many or as few virtual servers as needed.

explanation.summary: This describes EC2 scalability.
explanation.why: EC2 supports flexible provisioning and scaling of instances.

explanation.summary: Scalable computing is a core EC2 feature.
explanation.why: EC2 allows scaling compute capacity based on demand.

questions.question: What is the AWS Compute service that executes code only when triggered by events?

explanation.summary: AWS Lambda runs code in response to events without managing servers.
explanation.additionalInfo: Lambda is the canonical serverless compute service in AWS. Exams frequently frame it as event-driven and pay-per-use.

explanation.summary: CloudWatch is a monitoring service, not a compute service.
explanation.why: It collects metrics and logs but does not execute application code.

explanation.summary: Transit Gateway is a networking service.
explanation.why: It connects VPCs and networks but does not run code.

explanation.summary: EC2 requires provisioning and managing instances.
explanation.why: It does not execute code only on events and requires active servers.

questions.question: Both AWS and traditional IT distributors provide a wide range of virtual servers to meet their customers’ requirements. What is the name of these virtual servers in AWS?

explanation.summary: EBS snapshots are backups, not virtual servers.
explanation.why: Snapshots capture point-in-time copies of volumes and cannot function as compute resources.

explanation.summary: Amazon VPC is a networking service.
explanation.why: It provides isolated networking but does not represent virtual servers.

explanation.summary: AWS Managed Servers is not an official AWS service.
explanation.why: AWS does not use this terminology for compute resources.

explanation.summary: Amazon EC2 instances are AWS virtual servers.
explanation.additionalInfo: EC2 instances are the foundational compute units in AWS. Exams frequently refer to them as virtual servers when comparing AWS to traditional IT.

questions.question: What is the framework created by AWS Professional Services that helps organizations design a road map to successful cloud adoption?

explanation.summary: AWS Secrets Manager manages credentials and secrets.
explanation.why: It is a security service, not a cloud adoption framework.

explanation.summary: AWS WAF is a web application firewall.
explanation.why: It protects applications but does not guide cloud adoption strategy.

explanation.summary: The AWS Cloud Adoption Framework helps organizations plan cloud adoption.
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS CAF is frequently tested as the strategic framework for cloud adoption. It should not be confused with operational tools or security services.

explanation.summary: Amazon EFS is a file storage service.
explanation.why: It does not provide cloud adoption guidance.

questions.question: TYMO Cloud Corp is looking forward to migrating their entire on-premises data center to AWS. What tool can they use to perform a cost-benefit analysis of moving to the AWS Cloud?

explanation.summary: AWS Cost Explorer analyzes existing AWS spending.
explanation.why: It does not estimate or compare on-premises costs against AWS.

explanation.summary: The AWS Total Cost of Ownership Calculator compares on-premises costs with AWS.
explanation.additionalInfo: The AWS TCO Calculator is explicitly designed for cost-benefit analysis when migrating to AWS. Exams often contrast it with the Pricing Calculator.

explanation.summary: AWS Budgets monitors AWS spending after deployment.
explanation.why: It does not perform pre-migration cost comparisons.

explanation.summary: AWS Pricing Calculator estimates AWS service costs only.
explanation.why: It does not compare on-premises costs with AWS.

questions.question: Which of the following activities supports the Operational Excellence pillar of the AWS Well-Architected Framework?

options.text: Using AWS Trusted Advisor to find underutilized resources.

explanation.summary: Finding underutilized resources aligns more closely with cost optimization.
explanation.why: While useful, this activity primarily supports the Cost Optimization pillar rather than Operational Excellence.

options.text: Using AWS CloudTrail to record user activities.

explanation.summary: Recording user activity is mainly a security practice.
explanation.why: CloudTrail supports auditing and compliance rather than operational process improvement.

options.text: Using AWS CloudFormation to manage infrastructure as code.

explanation.summary: Infrastructure as code directly supports Operational Excellence.
explanation.additionalInfo: The Operational Excellence pillar emphasizes operations as code. CloudFormation is frequently tested as the canonical example of this principle.

options.text: Deploying an application in multiple Availability Zones.

explanation.summary: Multi-AZ deployments primarily support reliability.
explanation.why: This activity aligns with the Reliability pillar rather than Operational Excellence.

questions.question: Why do many startup companies prefer AWS over traditional on-premises solutions? (Choose TWO)

options.text: AWS allows them to pay later when their business succeed.

explanation.summary: AWS does not defer payments until a business succeeds.
explanation.why: AWS charges based on usage and does not offer delayed payment models for startups.

options.text: AWS can build complete data centers faster than any other Cloud provider.

explanation.summary: This statement is not a defined AWS benefit.
explanation.why: AWS does not market cloud adoption based on building physical data centers for customers.

options.text: Using AWS, they can reduce time-to-market by focusing on business activities rather than on building and managing data centers.

explanation.summary: AWS enables startups to focus on product development instead of infrastructure.
explanation.additionalInfo: Time-to-market reduction is a classic exam theme for startups choosing AWS over on-premises infrastructure.

options.text: AWS removes the need to invest in operational expenditure.

explanation.summary: AWS reduces capital expenditure, not operational expenditure.
explanation.why: Operational costs still exist, but are usage-based and variable.

options.text: Using AWS allows companies to replace large capital expenditure with low variable costs.

explanation.summary: AWS converts upfront capital costs into pay-as-you-go expenses.
keyPoints: Pay only for what is used
explanation.additionalInfo: Replacing CapEx with OpEx is one of the most frequently tested cloud benefits in AWS exams.

questions.question: What are the benefits of using DynamoDB? (Choose TWO)

options.text: Automatically scales to meet required throughput capacity.

explanation.summary: DynamoDB automatically scales to handle workload demand.
explanation.additionalInfo: Automatic scaling is one of DynamoDB’s primary differentiators and a frequent exam focus.

options.text: Provides resizable instances to match the current demand.

explanation.summary: DynamoDB does not use instances.
explanation.why: It is a serverless NoSQL service and does not expose instance sizing to customers.

options.text: Supports both relational and non-relational data models.

explanation.summary: DynamoDB is a non-relational database only.
explanation.why: It does not support relational schemas or SQL joins.

explanation.summary: DynamoDB provides consistent single-digit millisecond latency.
explanation.additionalInfo: Low latency is one of DynamoDB’s most tested characteristics, especially when compared to relational databases.

options.text: Supports the most popular NoSQL database engines such as CouchDB and MongoDB.

explanation.summary: DynamoDB is a proprietary NoSQL service.
explanation.why: It does not support third-party NoSQL engines.

questions.question: Which of the following can be used to protect data at rest on Amazon S3? (Choose TWO)

explanation.summary: S3 Versioning helps protect data from accidental deletion or overwrite.
explanation.additionalInfo: Versioning is frequently tested as a data protection mechanism rather than an encryption feature. It protects availability and integrity of data at rest.

explanation.summary: Amazon S3 does not provide deduplication as a security feature.
explanation.why: Deduplication is a storage optimization technique, not a method for protecting data at rest.

explanation.summary: S3 permissions control who can access data stored at rest.
keyPoints: Integrates with ACLs and bucket policies
explanation.additionalInfo: In exam context, data protection at rest includes access control. Permissions are therefore valid alongside encryption and versioning.

explanation.summary: Decryption is used to access encrypted data, not protect it.
explanation.why: Encryption protects data at rest, while decryption is the reverse operation.

explanation.summary: Conversion is unrelated to data protection.
explanation.why: It does not secure or control access to stored data.

questions.question: As part of the AWS Migration Acceleration Program (MAP), what does AWS provide to accelerate Enterprise adoption of AWS? (Choose TWO)

explanation.summary: AWS Partners help enterprises migrate and modernize workloads.
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS Partners are a core pillar of MAP and are frequently tested as part of migration acceleration support.

explanation.summary: AWS Artifact provides compliance reports.
explanation.why: It does not directly accelerate migrations or enterprise adoption.

explanation.summary: AWS Professional Services provides direct migration and transformation support.
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS Professional Services is explicitly included in MAP to help enterprises move faster and reduce migration risk.

explanation.summary: Athena is a query service.
explanation.why: It does not play a role in migration acceleration programs.

explanation.summary: Pinpoint is a customer engagement service.
explanation.why: It is unrelated to migration acceleration or enterprise adoption.

questions.question: AWS recommends some practices to help organizations avoid unexpected charges on their bill. Which of the following is NOT one of these practices?

options.text: Deleting unused EBS volumes after terminating an EC2instance.

explanation.summary: Deleting unused EBS volumes is a recommended cost-saving practice.
explanation.why: Unused volumes continue to incur charges if not deleted.

explanation.summary: Unused launch configurations do not incur charges.
keyPoints: No direct cost for launch configurations
Deleting them does not impact billing
explanation.additionalInfo: This option is commonly tested as a distractor. Launch configurations themselves are free and do not cause unexpected charges.

explanation.summary: Unused load balancers incur hourly charges.
explanation.why: Removing them helps prevent unnecessary billing.

options.text: Releasing unused Elastic IPs after terminating an EC2instance.

explanation.summary: Unused Elastic IPs incur charges.
explanation.why: Releasing them avoids unnecessary costs.

questions.question: What is the AWS tool that can help a company visualize their AWS spending in the last few months?

explanation.summary: AWS Cost Explorer provides visualizations of historical AWS spending.
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS Cost Explorer is specifically designed for visual cost analysis over time. Exams often contrast it with Budgets and Cost & Usage Reports.

explanation.summary: AWS Pricing Calculator estimates future AWS costs.
explanation.why: It does not visualize historical spending data.

explanation.summary: AWS Budgets focuses on alerts and thresholds.
explanation.why: It is used for monitoring against limits rather than visual historical analysis.

explanation.summary: Consolidated Billing combines charges across accounts.
explanation.why: It does not provide visualization tools.

questions.question: When running a workload in AWS, the customer is NOT responsible for: (Select TWO)

explanation.summary: Customers are responsible for testing their applications.
explanation.why: Penetration testing of customer workloads is allowed and remains a customer responsibility.

explanation.summary: Capacity reservation decisions are customer-driven.
explanation.why: Customers choose whether to reserve capacity using Reserved Instances or Savings Plans.

explanation.summary: AWS manages all physical data center operations.
explanation.additionalInfo: Under the shared responsibility model, AWS is always responsible for the physical data center layer.

explanation.summary: Customers are responsible for their own compliance obligations.
explanation.why: AWS provides compliance reports, but customers must meet regulatory requirements.

explanation.summary: AWS is responsible for securing the underlying infrastructure.
explanation.additionalInfo: Infrastructure security is always handled by AWS, while customers secure what they deploy on top of it.

questions.question: Which AWS service can be used to send promotional text messages (SMS) to more than 200 countries worldwide?

explanation.summary: Amazon SES is used for email delivery.
explanation.why: It does not support SMS messaging.

explanation.summary: Amazon S3 is a storage service.
explanation.why: It does not provide messaging capabilities.

explanation.summary: Amazon SNS supports global SMS messaging.
explanation.additionalInfo: Amazon SNS is the correct service for SMS messaging in AWS exams. It is often contrasted with SES and SQS.

explanation.summary: Amazon SQS is a message queue service.
explanation.why: It queues messages but does not send SMS messages.

questions.question: Which of the following allows you to create new RDS instances? (Choose TWO)

explanation.summary: AWS CodeDeploy is a deployment service.
explanation.why: It deploys application code but does not provision database instances.

explanation.summary: AWS Quick Starts provide reference architectures.
explanation.why: They are deployment guides and templates, not direct instance creation tools.

explanation.summary: AWS CloudFormation can provision RDS instances as infrastructure as code.
explanation.additionalInfo: CloudFormation is frequently tested as the primary infrastructure provisioning service for creating RDS instances programmatically.

explanation.summary: AWS DMS migrates databases.
explanation.why: It moves data between databases but does not create RDS instances.

explanation.summary: The AWS Management Console allows manual creation of RDS instances.
examples: Creating an RDS instance via console
explanation.additionalInfo: Exams often pair CloudFormation with the Management Console as valid ways to create RDS instances.

learnMore.title: Creating an Amazon RDS DB Instance

questions.question: One of the major advantages of using AWS is cost savings. What does AWS provide to reduce the cost of running Amazon EC2 instances?

explanation.summary: AWS does not charge a fixed monthly maintenance fee.
explanation.why: EC2 pricing is usage-based rather than flat maintenance costs.

explanation.summary: Tagging does not directly reduce compute costs.
explanation.why: Tags help track costs but do not lower EC2 pricing.

explanation.summary: AWS charges EC2 instances per second, reducing wasted compute costs.
explanation.additionalInfo: Per-second billing is a frequently tested cost optimization benefit of EC2 compared to traditional hourly billing models.

explanation.summary: AWS does not charge instance start-up fees.
explanation.why: There are no separate start-up costs for launching EC2 instances.

questions.question: Which AWS Group assists customers in achieving their desired business outcomes?

explanation.summary: The AWS Security Team focuses on AWS infrastructure security.
explanation.why: They do not directly assist customers with business outcome planning.

explanation.summary: AWS Professional Services helps customers achieve business outcomes.
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS Professional Services is commonly tested as the team that works directly with customers to achieve business and technical goals.

explanation.summary: Trusted Advisor provides recommendations.
explanation.why: It offers best practice checks but does not deliver business outcome engagements.

explanation.summary: Concierge Support focuses on billing and account support.
explanation.why: It does not assist with strategic business outcomes.

questions.question: Which AWS service or feature is used to manage the keys used to encrypt customer data?

explanation.summary: AWS Key Management Service (KMS) is used to create and manage encryption keys.
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS KMS is the standard service for managing encryption keys in AWS and is frequently tested in certification exams.

explanation.summary: Service Control Policies manage permissions, not encryption keys.
explanation.why: SCPs define account-level permission boundaries and do not handle cryptographic key management.

explanation.summary: MFA provides additional authentication security.
explanation.why: It protects access to resources but does not manage encryption keys.

explanation.summary: Amazon Macie discovers and classifies sensitive data.
explanation.why: It does not create or manage encryption keys.

questions.question: Which AWS Service allows customers to download AWS SOC & PCI reports?

explanation.summary: The Well-Architected Tool reviews workloads against best practices.
explanation.why: It does not provide compliance reports or audit documentation.

explanation.summary: AWS Artifact provides on-demand access to AWS compliance reports.
keyPoints: Access to SOC, PCI, ISO reports
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS Artifact is the authoritative source for AWS compliance and audit reports. Exams often test it directly for SOC and PCI access.

explanation.summary: AWS Glue is an ETL service.
explanation.why: It prepares and transforms data but does not manage compliance reports.

explanation.summary: Amazon Chime is a communications service.
explanation.why: It does not provide compliance or audit documentation.
